newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London untraded but look firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London untraded but look firm.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London did not trade on Friday due to the U.S. Independence Day holiday, but strategists said shares looked set to continue this week's record run on Wall Street.
The Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged this week and further evidence on Thursday of a moderate growth, low inflation picture for the U.S. economy should underpin stocks.
The Dow closed 100.43 points or 1.29 percent higher on Thursday at 7,895.81, after chalking up a record peak of 7,952.35.
The index gained 208 points in the shortened week.
"We had yet another week with no data that upsets this current best-case scenario of a soft landing on the U.S. economy," said Tim O'Dell, international strategist at UBS in London.
He said there was no threat of an imminent rate increase.
Next week's most crucial piece of U.S. data is Friday's June Producer Price Index (PPI), which is expected to be unchanged and bolster the prevailing low-inflation scenario, U.S. economists said.
The Labor Department reported on Thursday that payrolls rose by 217,000 in June, against expectations of a rise of 222,000, and that the unemployment rate ticked up to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent.
"All things being equal I would not expect (the U.S. stock markets) to go down next week and would rather be long than short as we sit now," said Nick Knight, head of strategy at Nomura.
U.S. stock, bond and foreign exchange markets will reopen on Monday July 7.
